text:
Through that door she fled saying: “Never!”
Through that door she must return one day…
When she closed that door she left cut short
the golden thread of my hope.
Through that door she must return one day.


Each time the impulse of the breeze,
like a weak, undecided hand,
lightly shakes the window,
my coward heart awaiting her
beats faster, faster.


From my worktable I see
the door my desires dream of
and my desire lurks crouched
in the trembling depth of my eyes.


For how long, solitary, elusive,
must I wait with uncertain gaze
for God, compassionate, to return to me
the woman who fled through that door?


When will those panes tremble,
pushed by her ducal hands,
and with her kiss arrive to them,
as in winter nights there comes to me
the pious kiss of a star?
O Lord, the pale one is already alert!
O Lord, evening falls now on my road
and my dead hope freezes!
O Lord, make the door open at last
and let my beloved enter through it!…
Through that door she must return one day!

translation.title: The Door
translation.editorial_note: This is a source variant of the previously reviewed “Through That Door” poem; the English wording is kept consistent with that earlier translation.
